missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Щека' is the feminine nominative subject of 'покраснела'. 'Левая' is the agreeing feminine adjective, and 'у ребёнка' is the genitive of possession. A simple description of a symptom.

missions.phrase: Бабушка нежно поцеловала меня в щёку.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Accusative of direction. 'В щёку' uses the feminine accusative 'щёку' after 'в' to show where the kiss lands. 'Меня' is the accusative of the person. The standard kiss-on-the-cheek pattern.
Strategic focus: Dative after 'по'. 'По щеке' uses the feminine dative 'щеке' to trace the path of the tear. 'Слеза' is the feminine nominative subject. Vivid and literary.
Strategic focus: Prepositional location. 'На щеке' uses the feminine prepositional 'щеке' after 'на' to place the dimple. 'У него' is the genitive of possession. A neat way to describe a face.

Strategic focus: Nominative plural subject. 'Щёки' is the feminine nominative plural subject of 'стали'. 'Горячими' is the instrumental predicate, and 'от стыда' is the genitive cause. Expressive for blushing.
Strategic focus: Accusative plural object. 'Щёки' is the feminine accusative plural object of 'надул'. The second verb 'засмеялся' continues the action. A playful, everyday image.
Strategic focus: Accusative plural object with dative. 'Щёки' is the feminine accusative plural object of 'пощипывал'. 'Нам' is the dative of the affected people. Classic Russian winter language.

missions.phrase: Цвет её щеки был очень нежным.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Genitive of relation. 'Щеки' is the feminine genitive after 'цвет', linking the colour to the cheek. 'Нежным' is the instrumental predicate. Useful for descriptive writing.
Strategic focus: Dative goal after 'к'. 'К щеке' uses the feminine dative 'щеке' to show where the ice goes. 'Лёд' is the masculine accusative object. A practical first-aid sentence.

missions.phrase: Эта щека немного опухла после удара.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Щека' is the feminine nominative subject of 'опухла'. 'Эта' points at a specific cheek, and 'после удара' is the genitive time frame. A natural injury description.
